[Interview, 2014-12-08, CNN TONIGHT]
HOST: They're on TV looking at themselves. He's like, is this water? What's going on here?
GUEST: Yes, you can have a drink. Don't feel nervous.

HOST: But do you think without this camera that there would be such an agreement that this was either a race or a class injustice, or whatever it is? You don't think it would be from multiple ethnicities?
GUEST: It was an injustice, period. Because again, there's black, white, Chinese. I have a store in front of my house, on the side of my building, and they're like, you know, we can't be out there to protest but, you know, we support you. We support you. They're like, you know, do you see the protests? Everybody texting me like did you see Paris? They were laying down in front of the Eiffel Tower, or did you see California? They were doing this, they were doing that. So it's just -- it's an everybody thing. You know, so it's like for celebrities to be like, you know, let's support the GUEST family because that was wrong, you know, it was wrong. So there's nothing they can do to make it right. But we can fight for justice so that it won't happen another time.

HOST: Yes. And the cat has Emery and Eric's tongue.

HOST: They didn't want to say -- they didn't want to say anything. It has been -- you said it wasn't a racial issue, and I think I saw you on television. Do you guys feel that -- because there's been people saying how can the family say this?

HOST: Do they let you speak? Are you guys OK?

HOST: It's been up and down for you, right?
GUEST: What do you all want to say? Like --

HOST: Yes, what do you want to say to the people?
GUEST: You know which of you.

HOST: And your name is Eric GUEST.

HOST: And that's going to -- that's going to follow you forever. People will remember your name forever.

HOST: What's that like having that name now?

[Interview, 2019-08-02, CNN NEWSROOM]
HOST: The police union president actually just finished a news conference as well. Here's what they said.

HOST: Eric, what would you say to him? And also just speak to his message to police officers, and, by the way, not just in New York City, but around the country.

HOST: Why?

HOST: Why?
